Cell Shield Lite never collects your data and cannot secretly change your phone. It only opens Android’s own screens and reads the list of installed apps.
Welcome

Cell Shield Lite is a guide, not a virus scanner.

It can:
• Check which apps use powerful permissions
• Tell you whether pop-up blocking (Private DNS) is on
• Open Android’s own screens for storage, backups and Play Protect

It does not collect any data and it cannot change your phone by itself. You stay in control.
What this app can and can’t do

CAN DO
• Check installed apps for powerful permissions (screen overlay, accessibility, reading text messages, installing apps)
• Show whether Private DNS pop-up blocking is turned on
• Take you straight to the Android screen to uninstall an app, clear browser data, free storage, back up, or open Play Protect

CANNOT DO
Android does not let an app you install from a link remove other apps by itself, read every app’s private data, or work as a full antivirus. Keep Google Play Protect turned on for malware scanning.

In the screen that opens, set Private DNS to a trusted blocker such as dns.adguard-dns.com. If a website’s \"I am not a robot\" check stops working, switch Private DNS back to Automatic for a few minutes.
Use this Android screen to see what is using space and remove files or unused apps.
Open your browser (Chrome, Samsung Internet, Firefox…), then choose Storage and cache to clear cached files and site data.
Turn on Google backup or your phone maker’s cloud backup before you clean anything up.
Make sure \"Scan apps with Play Protect\" is turned on. This is Android’s built-in malware scanner.
Good news: no installed apps stood out for powerful permissions. This is not a full virus scan, so keep Play Protect on as well.
Note: many trustworthy apps (password managers, screen readers, text-message apps) use these permissions on purpose. This is a prompt to check, not an accusation.
